# daterange.parse_range(text) -> (start, end)

Returns a pair of `datetime.date` (or None for an open end). Both ends are inclusive.

1. `A..B`, both ISO dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`): `(A, B)`.
2. `YYYY-MM`: the whole month, first to last day.
3. `YYYY-Www` (ISO week, e.g. `2026-W44`): Monday to Sunday of that ISO week.
4. `YYYY`: the whole year.
5. Open ends: `..B` is `(None, B)`, `A..` is `(A, None)`. `..` alone is an error.
6. `A..B` with B before A is an error.
7. Spaces around the text or around `..` are fine; anything else malformed (bad dates, `2026-13`, `2026-W54`, empty) is an error.

Errors raise `ValueError`.

Implemented `parse_range` in `daterange.py`: full-date ranges, month/week/year shorthand, open ends, whitespace tolerance, and `ValueError` for reversed or malformed input. Endpoints may mix forms; bare full dates and bare `..` are rejected.

Expanded `tests/test_daterange.py` to 25 cases covering every spec rule: leap February, month bounds, ISO weeks including week 53 and year-crossing weeks, standalone shorthands, open ends, reversed ranges, whitespace, and malformed inputs.

Verification: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q` passes all 25 tests.

END OF REPORT
